title: Generating Synthetic Households
text: Many synthetic population generation workflows produce individual agents generate household relationships needed simulation models. example, health-economic microsimulation models often require agents grouped households analysis can undertaken. replica package provides tools transforming agent-level synthetic population collection synthetic households preserving demographic geographic constraints. replica implements R port third-party python algorithm developed described Jan de Mooij, Tabea Sonnenschein, Marco Pellegrino, Mehdi Dastani, Dick Ettema, Brian Logan & Judith . Verstegen. Household generation replica based two core classes: HouseholdType HouseholdGrouper HouseholdType describes household structure generated, HouseholdGrouper applies one household definitions synthetic population. vignette demonstrates complete workflow creating synthetic households.

what: Supply a synthetic population of individual agents
title: Generating Synthetic Households
text: vignette assumes already created synthetic population individual agents. following code generates illustrative example population individual agents. simplicity, example contains four adults living neighbourhood. household_position column particularly important. Rather storing household membership directly, replica uses household-position categories indicate types roles agent may occupy within household. Examples include: Parent Child Grandparent Student positions subsequently referenced household types defined. example agents potential parents.
code: pop <- data.table(    agent_id = c(     "A001",     "A002",     "A003",     "A004"   ),    neighb_code = c(     "N1",     "N1",     "N1",     "N1"   ),    age = c(     40,     35,     50,     45   ),    gender = c(     "Male",     "Female",     "Male",     "Female"   ),    household_position = c(     "Parent",     "Parent",     "Parent",     "Parent"   )  )

title: Generating Synthetic Households
text: household type specifies household structure plan generate. create simple couple household. point defined household name. now need specify household members form household type.
code: hh <- HouseholdType(   "CoupleHousehold" )

title: Generating Synthetic Households
text: addMembers() method defines roles must filled constructing household. example, couple household requires two adults. tells replica : agents household position “Parent” eligible; agents represent “adult” household members; exactly two adults required per household. Notice two separate concepts used: household_position position_identifier household_position corresponds values appear synthetic population. position_identifier defines broader household roles used internally household-building algorithm. example, multiple population-specific household positions assigned identifier "adult". separation makes easier adapt household generation rules different source datasets. household definition now complete.
code: hh <- addMembers(   hh,   household_position = "Parent",   position_identifier = "adult",   amount = 2,   backup_position_identifiers = character() )

title: Generating Synthetic Households
text: Household construction often requires demographic matching rules. example: given household type, couples opposite-sex -sex? age differences used match partners? rules can specified using distributions. simplicity, illustrative example generate Female - Male pairs age gap partners within 5 years. age distribution indicates permissible partner age gaps range five years younger five years older.
code: hh@couple_gender_distribution <- c("Female|Male" = 1)  hh@couple_age_distribution <- c("-5-5" = 1)

title: Generating Synthetic Households
text: HouseholdGrouper coordinates household generation across entire synthetic population. group_by argument determines geographic administrative boundaries within household generation occur. example households generated independently within neighbourhood.
code: hg <- HouseholdGrouper(df_synth_pop = pop,                        group_by = "neighb_code")

title: Generating Synthetic Households
text: HouseholdGrouper may contain multiple household types. example, realistic population might contain: single-adult households; couple households; family households. Household types registered using addHouseholdType(). grouper now knows generate couple households.
code: hg <- addHouseholdType(hg,hh)

title: Generating Synthetic Households
text: household types registered, complete household-generation workflow can executed using run(). run() method executes complete household-generation workflow. grouping region (neighb_code example), replica: Identifies eligible household members. Creates household structures using registered HouseholdType objects. Matches adults according configured gender age distributions. Creates synthetic households. Assigns household identifiers. Produces household-level summary tables. result returned list containing agent-level household-level outputs.
code: result <- run(hg)

title: Generating Synthetic Households
text: result now contains agent-level household-level outputs. household-generation workflow produces two complementary outputs. synthetic_population contains one row per agent records household assignment synthetic individual. synthetic_households contains one row per household summarises resulting household structures. Together outputs allow analyses performed individual household level.
code: synthetic_population <- result$synthetic_population synthetic_households <- result$synthetic_households

title: Generating Synthetic Households
text: agent-level output now contains household identifiers. Agents sharing household identifier belong synthetic household.
code: synthetic_population[,c("agent_id", "household_id")] ##    agent_id household_id ##      <char>       <char> ## 1:     A001    SSH000001 ## 2:     A002    SSH000001 ## 3:     A003    SSH000002 ## 4:     A004    SSH000002

title: Generating Synthetic Households
text: household summary table provides one row per household. table often useful producing reports validating generated household structures.

title: Generating Synthetic Households
text: household-generation workflow automatically performs validation checks. Additional validation can performed manually. successful integrity check indicates : agents assigned ; eligible agents omitted; household membership records internally consistent.
code: any(   is.na(     synthetic_population$household_id   ) ) ## [1] FALSE

title: Generating Synthetic Households
text: previous example generated households containing adults . practice, many synthetic populations require complex household structures containing adults children. workflow can extended registering additional member roles. child household members present, replica automatically: forms sibling groups; creates adult partner groups; matches adults children; creates complete family households. additional user intervention required. resulting household structures stored using separate adult, child components.
code: hh <- HouseholdType("FamilyHousehold") hh <- addMembers(   hh,   household_position = "Parent",   position_identifier = "adult",   amount = 2,   backup_position_identifiers = character() )  hh <- addMembers(   hh,   household_position = "Child",   position_identifier = "child",   amount = 2,   backup_position_identifiers = character() )

title: Generating Synthetic Households
text: overall workflow can summarised : HouseholdType ↓ addMembers ↓ HouseholdGrouper ↓ addHouseholdType ↓ run ↓ Synthetic Population + Synthetic Households

title: Generating Synthetic Households
text: vignette : created synthetic population; defined household structure using HouseholdType; specified adult household members; configured demographic matching rules; registered household type using HouseholdGrouper; generated synthetic households using run(); explored agent-level household-level outputs. workflow can extended support multiple household types, family structures, complex demographic matching requirements.
